title: Resizing non-edge-touching Plasma Widget away from the edge it's not touching eventually cuts off opposite edge's shadow and removes rounded corner
line: Dragging the free edge of a panel widget's popup now makes it grow on that side, keeping its content and rounded corners intact.
explanation: While the user drags a popup's edge, KWin keeps the opposite edge fixed and ignores the position Plasma asks for, but on every resize the popup still computed a new position centred on its applet. Once that imagined position reached a screen edge, the popup dropped that side's border (square corner, no shadow) and the padding change made AppletPopup reset the window to its default size while KWin kept resizing, so the content shifted out of view. The resize handler now reports the dragged edges; until the popup is shown again it keeps the opposite edges where KWin keeps them, computes borders from that real geometry, and treats the size the user picked as explicit.

commits.message:
AppletPopup: keep the opposite edge in place while the user resizes

KWin ignores popup positions during a resize, but the popup was still
put back around its applet, so it drew borders for the wrong place and
by a screen edge reset its size. It now follows where KWin keeps it.

BUG: 504018

media.caption: Master: after dragging its left edge 300 px left the popup stays in place, the content shifts right and 'Open in File Manager' disappears.
Master: the top-right corner has become square.
Fixed: the same drag grows the popup to the left; content stays in place.
Fixed: the top-right corner stays rounded.

review.text: Accurate diagnosis and clean fix in libplasma for Wayland interactive popup resizing: WindowResizeHandler now emits resizeStarted(Qt::Edges), AppletPopup marks the size as explicitly set so padding changes no longer snap the window back to default mid-drag, and PopupPlasmaWindow keeps the opposite edges anchored to match KWin until the next Show event while computing borders from the real geometry. Verified across multiple edges, screen boundaries, and floating/non-floating panels with 11/11 libplasma tests passing.

reviews.text: Accurate diagnosis and clean fix in libplasma for Wayland interactive popup resizing: WindowResizeHandler now emits resizeStarted(Qt::Edges), AppletPopup marks the size as explicitly set so padding changes no longer snap the window back to default mid-drag, and PopupPlasmaWindow keeps the opposite edges anchored to match KWin until the next Show event while computing borders from the real geometry. Verified across multiple edges, screen boundaries, and floating/non-floating panels with 11/11 libplasma tests passing.

Sound diagnosis in the right layer: during an interactive resize KWin keeps the opposite edge fixed and ignores set positions, but PopupPlasmaWindow re-ran the applet-centred placement on every Resize event, so updateBorders worked on an imaginary rect, dropped the far border (square corner) and the padding change made AppletPopup::updateSize reset the size mid-drag. Tracking the dragged edges from WindowResizeHandler, deriving the real rect from the old size, clearing on Show and treating the user-picked size as explicit is a minimal, coherent fix; the screenshots show the popup growing left with content intact and the top-right corner rounded, and regressions (screen-edge drag, tray popup, floating panel, reopen) were checked. Nit only: the new protected PopupPlasmaWindow::setResizeEdges() adds exported API surface that could stay private (friend/d-pointer), and the resize edges stay set if startSystemResize() is refused, both harmless.
